adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 + app/models/post.rb:131 + app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — feed content stored with `cook_method: :raw_html` bypasses the sanitizing cook pipeline and is emitted via `raw post.cooked`, so unsanitized RSS/PollFeed HTML becomes stored XSS; run imported HTML through Sanitize before storing

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a bypass of the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline for imported content: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook returns `raw` directly for that method (skipping `post_analyzer.cook`). PollFeed passes `i.content` from the feed into `TopicEmbed.import` with only `CGI.unescapeHTML` and `scrub`, which do not sanitize unsafe HTML/attributes. The embed view then renders the result with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and for `:raw_html` posts `post.cooked == post.raw`, so any malicious HTML from the feed can be stored and emitted. This is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64-71 — `absolutize_urls` treats protocol-relative URLs as site-relative (`href.start_with?('/')` matches `//cdn.example.com/...` and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes), producing broken links/images; skip hrefs/srcs starting with `//` or use URI.join

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both link and image rewriting use `start_with?('/')` and then `sub(/^\/+/, '')`. A protocol-relative URL like `//cdn.example.com/a.png` starts with `/`, so it will be rewritten to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/a.png` (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/a.png`), which is incorrect/broken. The diff clearly introduces this behavior and the proposed fix (skip `//` or use `URI.join`) addresses it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32-37 — on the update path `embed.post` can be nil (no dependent: :destroy or FK), so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError and the uniquely-indexed embed_url can never be re-imported; guard on post.blank? and re-create or destroy the stale embed

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally instantiates `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the SHA changes. Since `topic_embeds.post_id` is not protected by any foreign key in the migration (only `null: false`) and there is no `dependent:` relationship shown to prevent orphaned `TopicEmbed` rows, it is possible for `topic_embeds` to reference a deleted/missing post. In that case `embed.post` returns `nil` and `PostRevisor` will later call methods on `@post` (e.g. `@post.acting_user` in `revise!`), raising a `NoMethodError`. Additionally, because `embed_url` is uniquely indexed, a stale/orphaned `TopicEmbed` row would block re-importing that URL unless handled. A guard/recovery is missing in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-30 — check-then-create on embed_url is not atomic against the new unique index, so concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs both create a topic and the loser's `TopicEmbed.create!` raises RecordNotUnique, orphaning a topic; rescue the uniqueness violation and retry the update path

adjudication.rationale:
TopicEmbed.import does a non-atomic `where(embed_url: url).first` then, if blank, creates a new Topic/Post and finally `TopicEmbed.create!` under a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. Two concurrent imports for the same URL (e.g., concurrent RetrieveTopic/PollFeed paths) can both see `embed.blank?` and both attempt `TopicEmbed.create!`; the loser will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`.

The proposed finding’s “orphaning a topic” part is likely overstated because the create happens inside a `Topic.transaction`, so the exception should roll back the topic/post too. However, the core race and unhandled uniqueness violation is a real, verifiable correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` relies on open-uri but topic_embed.rb never requires it, so Kernel#open can treat the URL as a filename and raise Errno::ENOENT; add `require 'open-uri'`

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`, the code calls `open(url).read` but the file does not `require 'open-uri'`. Without `open-uri`, Ruby’s `Kernel#open` will treat a string like `http://...` as a local path (or pipe) and typically raises `Errno::ENOENT`. While `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` does require `open-uri`, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` is also invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which does not require it, so this is a real, verifiable missing dependency in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 and app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `open()` calls lack :read_timeout/:open_timeout and any response-size cap, so a slow or huge remote page pins Sidekiq workers and starves the queue; pass explicit timeouts and bound the read

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two new network fetches using Ruby’s open-uri without any explicit limits: (1) `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and (2) `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read`. In both cases, there are no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options and no cap on how much data will be read into memory. Because these run in Sidekiq jobs (scheduled feed polling and async topic retrieval), a slow/hanging server or very large response can block a worker thread/process for a long time and/or consume excessive memory, reducing throughput and potentially starving the queue. This is a concrete robustness/security concern directly evidenced by the new `open(...)` calls in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the full feed download and import synchronously inside the retrieve job on every unknown embed URL, letting unauthenticated visitors trigger a full feed fetch/re-import; enqueue the poll instead of running it inline

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. This runs the feed download (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates/imports all feed items synchronously as part of handling an unknown embed URL, rather than enqueueing the scheduled job. Since the embed endpoint enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` even for `current_user` nil (EmbedController#best), any visitor who can hit /embed/best with a valid referer/host can indirectly cause a full feed fetch. The only throttle is per-embed-URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying the embed_url path can repeatedly trigger a full poll, making this a real performance/abuse risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — adding `force: true` to an already-shipped migration turns it into a destructive DROP TABLE top_topics on replay, silently destroying existing data; don't edit released migrations, add a new one instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. That turns what would have been a safe failure (exception if `top_topics` exists) into silent, destructive behavior that can wipe existing `top_topics` data if the migration is ever run against a DB where the table already exists (e.g., re-running/redoing migrations, restoring a DB and migrating, or other replay scenarios). Editing an older migration to add this behavior is a real data-loss risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255), but feed/article URLs regularly exceed 255 chars, raising StatementInvalid and rolling back the whole Topic.transaction so those imports fail permanently; use t.text with a hashed unique index or a much larger limit

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as `t.string`, which in Rails defaults to a 255-byte/varchar(255) column. The importing code (`TopicEmbed.import`) stores full article/feed URLs into `embed_url` and enforces uniqueness via a unique index on that column. If an incoming URL exceeds the column limit, the `TopicEmbed.create!` inside the `Topic.transaction` will raise (e.g., value too long / StatementInvalid) and roll back the transaction, causing the import to fail for that URL every time. This is a concrete failure mode introduced by the schema in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss and app/assets/javascripts/embed.js are not added to config.assets.precompile and the new 'embed' stylesheet isn't in any manifest, causing AssetNotPrecompiledError in production and 404s for embed.js; add both to the precompile list

lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-29 — `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `$redis.expire` is not atomic, so a crash between the calls leaves a throttle key with no expiry and permanently blocks that embed URL; use `SET key 1 NX EX 60`

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This is a well-known non-atomic pattern: if the process crashes or errors after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be left without a TTL, causing `setnx` to fail forever on future calls and permanently treating that `@embed_url` as "retrieved recently" (throttled). Nothing else in the diff ensures the TTL is set. Using an atomic `SET ... NX EX 60` (or a Lua script / MULTI) would avoid this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117,148 — the rewrite drops `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` and the `--category` option, so imported topics get import-time timestamps and no category, and it adds a live HTTP fetch per thread so a dead permalink raises out of import_remote and aborts the run mid-import

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` to stop creating topics via `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` and instead calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. This removes both the `--category` option (and all category assignment logic) and the explicit `created_at` override, so imported topics/posts will use the time of import and won’t be placed in a chosen category. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read` with no rescue; any HTTP/network error (dead permalink, timeout, etc.) will raise and can abort the import loop mid-run since `disqus.thor` doesn’t catch exceptions around that call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` rewrites the whole posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on Postgres < 11, causing multi-minute downtime; add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then set default/NOT NULL

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-NULL DEFAULT requires rewriting the entire table and takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock for the duration. Given this is the `posts` table (typically very large in production), the migration as written can cause significant downtime. This is a known, concrete behavior of Postgres migrations for this pattern, and the suggested safer approach (add nullable/no default, backfill, then set default + NOT NULL) addresses it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb — the spec only covers the three `execute` guard conditions, leaving `poll_feed` itself (feed parsing, i.link → i.id fallback, nil content, the TopicEmbed.import call) with zero coverage; add a spec that parses a fixture feed

adjudication.rationale: This is verifiable from the diff: `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts the `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` guard conditions and that it delegates to `poll_feed` when settings are present. It does not test `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` itself (the `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` call, `i.link` fallback to `i.id`, `i.content` handling/scrub/unescape, or that `TopicEmbed.import` is invoked with the expected arguments). So the core behavior added in `poll_feed` has no direct spec coverage in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5,12 — `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` is not null-checked before `comments.appendChild(iframe)`, so the script throws when the container is missing or not yet in the DOM

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is assigned from `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and is used immediately in `comments.appendChild(iframe);` without checking for null. Because the IIFE runs immediately when the script is evaluated, if the element with id `discourse-comments` is missing or the script executes before that element exists in the DOM, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a runtime error. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` is concatenated with no separator, producing URLs like `https://forum.example.comembed/best` when the configured URL lacks a trailing slash

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the iframe URL is built as `discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...` with no guaranteed `/` between `discourseUrl` and `embed/best`. Since `discourseUrl` is an external/global configuration value (/* global discourseUrl */) and the code does not normalize it to include a trailing slash, a value like `https://forum.example.com` will indeed produce the broken URL `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`.
